h1: The 6 Best Smart Speakers With Screens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six smart displays from Amazon and Google, sorted by screen size, sound, camera options and smart home reach.
summary: The Echo Show 8 is the best smart display for most homes, balancing a 8.7 inch screen, spatial audio and a mid-range price. The Echo Show 11 is the upgrade for bigger rooms, the Echo Show 5 fits bedside tables, and the Nest Hub is the camera free pick for Google households. The Echo Hub is the one to buy if you want a wall panel for smart home control rather than a speaker.
intro: Buyers often pick a smart display by screen size alone, then discover the real decision is the ecosystem. An Echo Show will not behave like a Nest Hub, and your existing smart plugs, lights and music subscriptions will quietly decide which one feels useful on day two.

Six displays are covered here, judged on their spec sheets and the feedback of people who use them every day. We ranked them on screen size, audio, camera and privacy options, smart home protocol support and how well each fits the room it is meant for. The Echo Spot and the renewed Nest Hub Max were left out as narrower or less certain buys.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 8 (newest model), Vibrant HD 8.7" Display with Spatial Audio, Designed for Alexa+, Graphite
products.verdict: The right size, the right sound and a sensible price for almost any room.
products.description:
The Echo Show 8 has an 8.7 inch HD display with spatial audio and is designed for Alexa+. It is the middle step in Amazon's lineup and the size most kitchens and living rooms can absorb without it dominating a counter.

It ranks first because it avoids the compromises at either end. The Show 5 below is smaller with less room for recipes and video, while the Show 11 above costs noticeably more for screen area many rooms never use. Spatial audio also gives it a fuller sound than the smaller models.

Buy it if you want one display that works for cooking, video calls and music. The caveat is that it is tied to Amazon's ecosystem, so Google service users will be happier elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Most homes wanting one versatile smart display.
products.skipIf: Your household runs on Google services.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 11 (newest model), Vibrant Full-HD 11" Display with Spatial Audio, Designed for Alexa+, Graphite
products.verdict: The newest Echo display, with an 11 inch Full HD screen for bigger rooms.
products.description:
The Echo Show 11 pairs an 11 inch Full HD display with spatial audio and Alexa+. It is Amazon's newest 2025 model in the standard Show range and has the sharpest screen of the countertop displays here.

It sits just behind the Show 8 because the price steps up into a higher bracket, and the extra screen area only pays off when you will view it from across a room. If you do, the Full HD panel makes photos and video clearly better.

It suits open plan spaces and buyers who want the current generation. If your counter space is tight, the Show 8 is the safer fit.
products.idealFor: Open plan rooms and photo or video fans.
products.skipIf: You have a small counter or bedside table.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 5 (newest model), Smart Display, Designed for Alexa+, Charcoal
products.verdict: The small display that fits a nightstand without crowding it.
products.description:
The Echo Show 5 has a 5.5 inch display, Alexa+ built in and double the bass of the previous generation. It is the smallest standard Show and one of the cheapest ways into Alexa with a screen, priced under $100.

It ranks third because the small screen limits what you can do with recipes, video and smart home dashboards. In return it fits places the Show 8 cannot, like a bedside table or a crowded desk.

It suits bedrooms, offices and anyone who mainly wants alarms, weather and music. If you plan to watch video often, step up to the Show 8.
pros: Twice the bass of prior model
products.skipIf: You want to follow recipes or watch video.

products.name: Google Nest Hub 7" Smart Display with Google Assistant (2nd Gen), Chalk
products.verdict: A camera free Google display with sleep sensing for bedrooms.
products.description:
The second generation Nest Hub has a 7 inch display, Google Assistant and no camera. It also includes Sleep Sensing, a bedroom feature that tracks your sleep without a lens on the device.

It ranks fourth because the Amazon displays above offer more screen sizes and newer assistant branding. What it gives you instead is a clear privacy story, since there is simply no camera to worry about, and strong fit for households already using Google services.

Choose it for a bedroom or kitchen in a Google home. If you want video calls, look at a camera equipped display instead.
products.idealFor: Google households that value camera free privacy.
products.skipIf: You need video calls or Alexa.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 15 (newest model), Full HD 15.6" Kitchen Hub with Built-In Fire TV, Designed for Alexa+
products.verdict: A wall mount sized kitchen hub with Fire TV built in.
products.description:
The Echo Show 15 is a 15.6 inch Full HD display built as a kitchen hub, with Fire TV included. It acts as a family organizer and a small TV in one panel.

It ranks fifth because the size is a commitment. It needs a wall or a large counter spot, which makes it the wrong choice for most small spaces despite being the most capable screen here for entertainment.

Buy it if you have a dedicated wall in a busy kitchen and want recipes, schedules and streaming in one place. Skip it if you are tight on space or want something portable.
products.idealFor: Busy family kitchens with a free wall.

products.name: Amazon Echo Hub (newest model), 8", Zigbee, Matter, Thread, Compatible with Thousands of Devices
products.verdict: A smart home control panel, not a media speaker.
products.description:
The Echo Hub is an 8 inch panel with Zigbee, Matter and Thread support and no camera. It is designed to control lights, locks and thermostats from a wall rather than to play music or take calls.

It ranks last in a speaker ranking because audio and video are not its job. For smart home builders, though, native support for those three protocols is the reason to buy it over any display above.

Choose it if you run a lot of connected devices and want a dedicated dashboard. If you want a general purpose display, buy the Show 8 instead.
products.idealFor: Smart home owners wanting a control dashboard.
products.skipIf: You want music or video calls.

whatMatters.detail: A smart display is the front end for either Alexa or Google Assistant, so your existing accounts and devices matter more than the hardware. Switching later means re-adding every light and speaker. Check which assistant your current smart plugs and music service work best with before you buy.

Sizes here range from 5.5 inches to 15.6 inches. Small screens work for alarms and glances, while video and recipes need 8 inches or more. Think about viewing distance, and match the display to the room using the size in the listing title.

Some displays carry a camera for video calls, while the Nest Hub and Echo Hub do not. A camera adds convenience but also a privacy question for bedrooms. Read the listing for a camera line, and prefer a camera free model for sleeping spaces.

Matter, Thread and Zigbee are the standards many modern devices use to talk to a hub. A display that supports them can control more gear without extra bridges. The Echo Hub lists all three in its title, so check for them if you own many connected devices.

A smart display is still a speaker, and small ones sound thin. Spatial audio and extra bass on a larger cabinet help music fill a room. Look for audio features named in the listing rather than vague words like rich sound.

faq.q: Can I mix Alexa and Google displays in one home?
faq.a: You can, but they will not share routines or device control. Pick one assistant for the devices you use most and add a second only for a specific room.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a smart display?
faq.a: Choosing by screen size before checking the ecosystem. If your smart plugs and music service favor the other assistant, the display will feel limited.

faq.q: Is the Echo Show 11 worth it over the Show 8?
faq.a: Only if you view the screen from across the room or care about Full HD photos. For counters and desks, the Show 8 gives most of the experience for less.

faq.q: Do I need a hub if I buy the Echo Hub?
faq.a: The Echo Hub lists Zigbee, Matter and Thread support, so it can act as the hub for many compatible devices without a separate bridge.

faq.q: Where should I place a smart display?
faq.a: Keep it near a power outlet and within Wi Fi range, away from steam and direct sunlight. A shelf at eye level works best.

faq.q: Can a display with no camera still make calls?
faq.a: Audio calls may work through the assistant, but video calling needs a camera. Camera free models like the Nest Hub are not suited to video chat.

finalTake: For most people the Echo Show 8 is the display to buy. Move up to the Echo Show 11 for a large room, down to the Echo Show 5 for a nightstand, or to the Nest Hub if you live in the Google world. Buy the Echo Hub only if a smart home control panel is the actual goal.
